faq.a: Pongal is a four-day harvest festival in Tamil Nadu, India, in mid-January. Families boil new rice with milk and jaggery until it overflows, decorate with kolam patterns and honour the cattle who help on farms.

faq.q: What is the New Yam Festival?
faq.a: It is a harvest festival of the Igbo people of Nigeria, usually in August. People give thanks for the yam harvest and share the first new yams with music, dancing and masquerades.

faq.q: Why do some harvest festivals follow the moon?
faq.a: Many farming calendars were based on the moon. The full moon nearest autumn, the harvest moon, gave extra light for gathering crops, so festivals like Chuseok and Mid-Autumn fall then.
A celebration when crops have been gathered, to give thanks for food and share it with family, friends and people in need.
Sukkot is a week-long Jewish harvest festival in autumn. Families build a sukkah, a hut with a leafy roof, and eat meals in it.
asks: Why do Jewish families build a hut?

facts: The word Pongal means boiling over, after the rice pot that is allowed to overflow.
Homowo, the harvest festival of the Ga people of Ghana, means hooting at hunger.
